Audited chat/generation token capacities were verified against primary sources on 2026-09-19. Shared context, independent input, and output are distinct; missing maxima, adjustable defaults and configuration-only values are never fabricated into capacities.

Legacy aliases, model IDs and qualitative capabilities remain compatible. Only verifiedAliases and exact IDs are appropriate for numeric matching; deployment labels and family/prefix heuristics are not evidence.

Root limits describe publisher-native specifications or checkpoint capacity, not every hosting deployment. Apply generic host profiles before more specific protocol/version profiles; explicit null clears inherited capacity. Retired snapshots preserve historical evidence without asserting cross-host retirement.
OpenAI coverage includes GPT-5.x model IDs seen through Foundry, older Responses orchestration models, and direct GPT Image models.

Image-generation tool metadata was checked against official model-specific Supported tools documentation on 2026-09-08. Generic function calling, image input, and inclusion in a Responses model list alone do not establish hosted image-generation support; a false or omitted flag means it is not verified for this integration.

OpenAI model pages describe api.openai.com, not Azure deployment readiness. Azure requires its v1 Responses surface for the hosted image tool; the dated 2025-04-01-preview Responses contract is not equivalent to v1. Direct Images API versions are a separate contract.

Azure lists GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna version 2026-07-09 for Responses. Its image-tool examples may require a deployed GPT Image backend and the x-ms-oai-image-generation-deployment header. Catalog support does not promise deployment-free routing, entitlement, region availability, or a successful live request.

Azure -chat entries are not automatically equated with OpenAI -chat-latest model IDs. OpenAI's documented tools for a similarly named chat snapshot do not establish the Azure entry's image tool support.

Capabilities classify model behavior, not live availability. New legacy/deprecated/retired entries describe the cited API lifecycle; OpenAI retirement dates do not automatically apply to Azure. Retained DALL-E compatibility must not be interpreted as an operational service.

The original OpenAI boolean capability subset covers GPT-5.x model families, including Azure OpenAI IDs seen through Foundry. Additional operation records cover older chat and image models; reasoning-only entries cover legacy GPT and o-series policies without declaring capabilities.

Reasoning policies describe effort support, not endpoint/API availability. No Responses API migration is implied. Responses-only max effort is excluded from this Chat Completions policy. Models without verified level lists remain unknown.

Embedding specifications and aliases were checked against primary sources on 2026-09-16. OpenAI embeddings use cl100k_base; text-embedding-ada-002 version 1 accepts 2,046 tokens, while version 2 and text-embedding-3 accept 8,192. Uncataloged Ada version metadata requires explicit administrator-verified limits rather than inheriting a newer version's context.

Cohere model knowledge does not establish a supported current OpenAI-compatible embeddings route. Its task-sensitive native APIs and the deprecated Azure Model Inference API are not implemented. An explicit compatible-gateway declaration must attest that the gateway handles input_type and any dimensions translation; SimpleChat never sends vendor-native fields to a standard OpenAI operation.

Azure lists embed-v-4-0 with a 512-token hosting limit; Cohere lists embed-v4.0 with 128k model context. The default policy retains the 512-token Azure limit and records 128,000 separately as model_context_tokens. A larger verified hosting limit must be declared explicitly, never inferred from the model context.

Cohere batch count is bounded by its documented 96-text limit. The 49,152-token default batch budget is a conservative application bound derived from 96 inputs of 512 tokens, not a claim about a vendor aggregate-token limit.

The 2026-09-19 token audit covers the original 75 records with tokenLimitEvidence. Additional qualitative and reasoning-only records omit unreviewed token fields and qualitative flags rather than guessing them. Embedding policies preserve their sourced dimensions, hosting/version input limits, and application batch budgets separately from chat context, generation limits, accounting, and verified numeric aliases.

Historical source review dates remain independent: reasoning metadata on 2026-09-07, image-tool metadata on 2026-09-08, and embedding metadata on 2026-09-16. These retained dates do not claim a new source review or a chat-token audit of the additional models.

The 2026-09-19 token-capacity audit covers the original 75 records with tokenLimitEvidence. Operation-only records retain documented qualitative flags without token limits, accounting, profiles, or numeric aliases; reasoning-only records retain only their policy and identifiers. Missing limits and flags remain unknown, not inferred from an operation or policy.

Historical React V2 source review dates are retained independently: reasoning metadata on 2026-09-07, image-tool metadata on 2026-09-08, and provider-qualified image profiles on 2026-09-16. These dates do not claim a new source review or a token-capacity audit of the additional models.

OpenAI model pages describe api.openai.com, not Azure deployment readiness. imageProfiles separates direct OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and Foundry image operations. The application hosting cloud never establishes endpoint capabilities or availability.

Azure documents Responses image generation with a separate GPT Image deployment. SimpleChat deliberately offers only dedicated image models on Azure/Foundry; the conditional Azure Responses integration is not enabled by publisher imageGenerationTool flags or administrator overrides.

Government image-model availability is not established by the reviewed Government model table. Unknown is not unavailable, and a Government-hosted app may use an explicitly configured commercial endpoint without relabeling that endpoint as Government.

Image operation profiles describe the implemented single-image workflow. MAI and FLUX support source-image edits where stated, but their reviewed APIs do not document uploaded masks. Masking is not inferred from vision, tool calling, or inpainting prose.
